statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-95691 ("Retransmitted QUIC CRYPTO Frames Can Cause DoS or One-byte Disclosure", Low) affects OpenSSL 3.5 and is fixed on the openssl-3.5 branch for OpenSSL 3.5.10, which is not released yet: https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20261110.txt, fix https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/f6244675833e097c2429a40d1b206d95385bd42f, which keeps the CRYPTO stream range lent to the TLS record layer locked until it is released. The published DHI Alpine 3.23 openssl builds are 3.5.4-r0, 3.5.5-r0, 3.5.5_git20260330-r1, 3.5.6-r0, 3.5.6-r1, 3.5.7-r0, 3.5.7-r1, 3.5.8-r0, 3.5.8-r1, 3.5.9-r0, 3.5.9-r1 and 3.5.9-r2; we checked the libcrypto3 and libssl3 packages of each on x86_64 and aarch64 against the debug symbols in the openssl-dbg package of the same build, matched by build ID, each package verified against the index checksum. 3.5.9-r2 is OpenSSL 3.5.9 rebuilt with that commit applied: on x86_64 and aarch64 its libssl.so.3 contains ossl_sframe_set_lock_range() and ossl_sframe_set_unlock_range(), the functions the commit adds, which 3.5.9-r0 and 3.5.9-r1 do not. No earlier build, including 3.5.9-r1, has either function on either architecture. Alpine lists the fix in its own 3.5.9-r1: https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-95691 and https://secdb.alpinelinux.org/v3.23/main.json, but the DHI Alpine 3.23 build numbered 3.5.9-r1 does not carry it, so 3.5.9-r2 is the first fixed DHI build. The openssl-fips packages built from the same source hold the FIPS provider fips.so, whose debug symbols in openssl-dbg have no ossl_quic_ or ossl_sframe_ function in any build.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-95691 ("Retransmitted QUIC CRYPTO Frames Can Cause DoS or One-byte Disclosure", Low) affects OpenSSL 3.5 and is fixed on the openssl-3.5 branch for OpenSSL 3.5.10, which is not released yet: https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20261110.txt, fix https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/f6244675833e097c2429a40d1b206d95385bd42f, which keeps the CRYPTO stream range lent to the TLS record layer locked until it is released. Debian lists trixie as vulnerable with no fixed version: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-95691. DHI backports that commit into its standard Debian 13 openssl builds, starting with the second DHI build of 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and in every later standard build: the third and fourth DHI builds of 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and both DHI builds of 3.5.9-1~deb13u1. On amd64 and arm64 those builds' libssl3t64 has ossl_sframe_set_lock_range() and ossl_sframe_set_unlock_range(), the functions the commit adds, in libssl.so.3, read from the libssl3t64-dbgsym debug symbols matched by build ID; we checked the libssl3t64 package of every published Debian 13 openssl build on both architectures, each verified against the index SHA256. Their changelogs also carry the backport entry. Every earlier standard build has neither of those functions and no changelog entry for this CVE: Debian has not shipped the fix, and DHI added the backport with the second 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 build. The FIPS builds of openssl (the +fips versions in the DHI security repository) are affected: the FIPS build is pinned to the validated upstream release and does not take this backport. Every FIPS build's libssl3t64 has neither of those functions on both architectures, and their changelogs have no entry for this CVE. The advisory's "FIPS impact: no" covers the FIPS provider module only; the affected code is in libssl, which the FIPS builds ship without the fix. The FIPS provider fips.so in every published openssl-provider-fips package has no ossl_quic_ or ossl_sframe_ function, read from its openssl-provider-fips-dbgsym debug symbols matched by build ID. A FIPS build sorts above the standard builds of the same Debian version, so the range has three affected spans: every build below the first fixed 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 build, the 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 FIPS build up to the first 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 build, and the 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 FIPS build onward.
